gap: No result ChatGPT got names one store where a matched 48V battery and inverter/charger go into a single cart. Sun Gold Power sells both: the SPH6548P 6.5 kW split-phase inverter at $1,035 plus the SG48100P 51.2V 100Ah UL1973/UL9540A server-rack battery at $981, $2,016 together. The battery's own page lists SunGoldPower among the inverters it talks to over CAN/RS485. The same store's 6000W low-frequency inverter needs a 240VAC input to charge.
standout_why: Both ChatGPT chats got an empty result list and cited no pages, so there were no rival pages to read. Compared with its two answers: they give only price ranges ('$700–$1,300' battery, '$500–$2,000' inverter, 'not verified current quotes'). They say 'mutually compatible equipment' and 'EG4, Sol-Ark, or Victron' without naming a pair that shares a communication protocol. They name no store that sells both halves and never say an inverter's charger may need 240VAC input. They do already say that approved transfer or isolation equipment and an electrician are needed for panel connections, so that is not new.
kit_items: 48V LiFePO4 battery: Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2V 100Ah server rack. Its store page says UL1973 and UL9540A and lists 'CAN/RS485/RS232 … compatible with … SunGoldPower', so it pairs with the same brand's inverter in one cart.

Inverter/charger: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P 6.5 kW 48V split-phase. Its store page says it accepts '48V … Lithium batteries' and outputs 'Split phase (120V/240V) or Single phase (120v)', and that it is UL 1741 by ETL. It costs less than the same store's 6000W low-frequency unit, whose page says it 'requires 240VAC input'.
Same-store alternative: Vatrer 48V 5000W Solar Inverter with MPPT plus a Vatrer 48V 100Ah wall-mounted LiFePO4 (CAN/RS485, per its page), $1,699.98 in one Vatrer cart.
Not in any approved cart: DC breaker or fuse, a transfer switch or interlock at the panel, and an electrician. ChatGPT's answers already say these are needed.
